displayPattern: Dual 7-segment display on a Rheem R96V / (-)96V furnace (installation instructions 92-24161-124-03): d6
meaning: Horsepower conflict on the memory card. The motor's horsepower does not match the card, but the model data in the furnace control does match the motor. This is a non-critical fault, shown in standby.
causes: Blower motor was replaced with the wrong horsepower
Memory card or furnace control was replaced with the wrong part
diySteps: If the furnace is running and d6 appears only in standby, the manual says operation should proceed as normal

Technician: determine the correct motor and model-data card and replace the incorrect part. The manual says the original card must be used when it is available, and a card from another furnace can damage the heat exchanger
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician before anyone replaces the blower motor or the memory card. d6 is a parts-match fault, not a lockout.
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
sourceTitle: Rheem (-)96V series installation instructions 92-24161-124-03, Table 20 R96V fault codes. Read 2026-11-07
